overall_note: The orchestrator's uv.toml remedy (amendment 9d06fdfe21) was mechanically sound for a plain project — on-box probes PROVED ancestor-discovery works there (baseline nlink=2 -> ancestor-uv.toml nlink=1; strict TOML schema rejection confirmed; top-level link-mode documented in uv help sync) — but the candidate repository itself defeats it: astrid-first's committed pyproject.toml contains a [tool.uv] table, and with ANY [tool.uv] present uv 0.12.5 stops merging ancestor uv.toml files above the project boundary. Isolation is tri-variate and decisive: synthetic p1 without [tool.uv] links=1, p2 with comment-only [tool.uv] links=2 (ancestor ignored), p3 with [tool.uv] carrying explicit link-mode="copy" links=1; full flow-env replicas all honor the ancestor config (links=1), and a read-only-tree sync against the actual dead worktree reproduces links=2. Consequence: the single S9 attempt died EXACTLY where T74RESUME3 attempt 2 died — hardlink_unsupported at phase=snapshot on generation 05b40a47e3e6b501 (same mypyc .so, nlink=2) — with runtime-create again proving the audioop-lts marker wall fixed under uv. Both card halt-prongs triggered (uv.toml effectively ignored for THIS candidate AND snapshot still fails); per card directive, halted honestly after recording, no further remedies improvised. Every escape hatch remains outside task authority: placing uv.toml inside the sandbox project root is impossible before a build because arnold-canary-build refuses non-empty roots (root_not_fresh) and post-clone injection has no hook; an in-tree uv.toml/[tool.uv] edit is a staged-candidate change; UV_LINK_MODE env plumbing is candidate code; /etc/uv is outside disposable roots; weakening take_snapshot is a ratified-contract change.

Conclusion: candidate-repo CONTENT ([tool.uv] presence) x uv project-config-boundary precedence deterministically neutralizes ancestor uv.toml discovery for THIS candidate. The remedy was correct for a plain project and structurally inapplicable here.
